title: An inbox item that fails at triage (F4 protected-surface rejection) is re-claimed by a lane in EVERY wave — no per-item consecutive-failure breaker; 5+ lanes of the 2026-09-14 batch burned on one item
evidence: Batch loop-20260913-fresh-4: waves 0-6 = 0/3, 0/3, 2/3, 2/3, 1/3, 1/3, 0/3 lanes ok. Cycles 1664, 1668, 1670 (and the same shape in 1661/1665/1669/1672) ended `ORCHESTRATOR_CYCLE_FAILED … phases_run=2` after `ORCHESTRATOR_PHASE_VERDICT_FAIL phase=triage — triage verdict=FAIL: top_n card "nonconforming-deliverable-settle-wait-latency" names protected s[urface]`.

The item (2026-07-19T02-00-00Z-…, weight 0.85, files []) is dispatchable to lanes (inboxbatch.ConsoleRouted routes on route:console-* or a protected path in files[] — this item declares neither), but every lane's triage discovers the protected surface and FAILs; the claim is released and the next lane picks it again. Mitigation applied: the item is now route:console-manual.
There is no per-item breaker on repeated claim→FAIL (grep core/triage*.go, cyclerun_select.go: none); the contract-gate breaker and the identical-fingerprint halt do not cover this class.
acceptance: After N (policy, default 2) consecutive cycles that claim an item and FAIL before build, the loop parks the item (inbox-parked/ with a named reason and the failing cycles) and emits an inbox.warning code naming the item — never a silent re-pick.
Triage's F4 rejection (a top_n card naming a protected surface) routes the item to console immediately (set route:console-manual on the record with the reason) instead of leaving it dispatchable.
A regression test drives two lanes over the same protected-surface item and asserts the second lane never claims it.
notes: Pipeline-integrity class; the 2-consecutive-zero-ship rule fired on this batch (waves 0-1 and wave 6) — this item is the dominant cause. Filed while landing ADR-0103 units before the verification wave.
